findings.what: The wave rule (DECISIONS.md §1.6: "Every lane mock declares its RPC verbs; shared verbs are declared shared") and the brief's own shared-file instruction (brief-646.md:101: declare every RPC verb your mock answers, marking as shared any verb the documents-viewer lane also answers) are not actually satisfied by an enforced declaration — only by prose comments that are themselves false as shipped. `document-correction-mock.mjs` dispatches RPCs via `const rpc = path.slice(...); if (rpc === "...")`, a fourth spelling the census's `RPC_VERB_OPENER` regex (`verb === "..."` | `fn === "..."` | `path === "/rest/v1/rpc/..."`) does not recognise. So `rpcVerbCensus()` never sees any of this file's verbs, and the 'verb-ownership census' test (line 1026) that is supposed to fail on an undeclared shared verb is structurally blind to this whole lane. Four verbs are actually answered by BOTH `document-correction-mock.mjs` and `documents-viewer-mock.mjs` (`get_document_state`, `get_document_extract`, `list_source_revisions`, `list_source_dependents`), and none is present in `SHARED_RPC_VERBS` (lines 973-1005) — confirmed by grep. Yet the code comments claim the opposite: document-correction-mock.mjs:8-10 and documents-viewer-mock.mjs:540-544 both say the two lanes' shared verbs are 'declared as shared in e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts', and commit 1d042586's own message says '…declared SHARED in e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts, whose N5 census is green with the new lane registered (15/15)' — none of which is true (there is no such declaration, and the census that would prove it never runs against this file). Both mocks happen to scope correctly today (each falls through on a foreign document id), so there is no live e2e bug, but the safety net the house rule and LENS both require — a census that fails loud on an undeclared/unsafe share — is inert for this ticket's lane, and the report's whole-suite pass count implicitly relies on it as proof.
findings.evidence: grep -rln 'get_document_extract"' apps/web/e2e/*.mjs -> document-correction-mock.mjs and documents-viewer-mock.mjs both match (also get_document_state, list_source_revisions, list_source_dependents). `node -e` reproduction of the exact RPC_VERB_OPENER regex against document-correction-mock.mjs returns 0 matches. Running `node --import ./test/bootstrap.mjs --import tsx --test e2e/e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts` prints '65 distinct RPC verb(s) censused; 5 answered by more than one lane mock' — the list names get_document_state/list_review_queue/get_work_plan_origin/list_entry_links/list_spoken_for_documents only, no #646 lane and no fourth or fifth entry — yet the test still reports 15/15 pass, i.e. it passes without ever asserting the property this ticket's own comments and commit message claim it asserts.
findings.fix: Rename the dispatch variable in document-correction-mock.mjs from `rpc` to `verb` (matching documents-viewer-mock.mjs's own convention) so the existing census picks it up — or add a fourth alternative to RPC_VERB_OPENER for `rpc === "..."`. Then add the four real collisions to SHARED_RPC_VERBS, sorted to match rpcVerbCensus's `[...set].sort()`: `get_document_extract: ["document-correction-mock.mjs", "documents-viewer-mock.mjs"]`, `get_document_state: ["document-correction-mock.mjs", "documents-viewer-mock.mjs", "work-list-mock.mjs"]` (widening the existing 2-lane entry), `list_source_dependents: ["document-correction-mock.mjs", "documents-viewer-mock.mjs"]`, `list_source_revisions: ["document-correction-mock.mjs", "documents-viewer-mock.mjs"]`. Re-run e2e-fixture-ownership.test.ts and confirm the census now reports 9 shared verbs, all declared, before re-claiming the house rule is satisfied.
